_comment: Per-area line-coverage floors, enforced by tools/check-coverage.py via
Per-area rather than one global number, deliberately. The tree sat at 74.4%
0 of 11 functions executed — a global target is satisfied by
workspace/registries at 96% and says nothing about the surface the product is
built around. A floor per area is what makes a specific area rotting visible.
Floors are set a few points under the measured value at the time they were
recorded, so ordinary churn does not trip them but a real drop does. Raise a
floor when an area improves; lowering one needs a reason in the commit
message, exactly like moving a perf baseline.
Recorded 2026-08-04 on the commit that added the merge-surface paint tests.
